headline: Atlanta's new pandas are out of quarantine. Fans flocked.
summary: Ping Ping and Fu Shuang, both six years old, made their public debut at Zoo Atlanta. They arrived in late September and spent their first weeks in quarantine. They are on loan from China under a six-year agreement. Zoo Atlanta is now one of three US zoos with giant pandas, with San Diego and the National Zoo in Washington.
cover_answer: They weren't. New animals get quiet weeks to settle in.
table_question: Should a new kid get a few quiet weeks before everyone crowds in?

5-7.script: Two pandas named Ping Ping and Fu Shuang came out to meet people at the zoo in Atlanta. They are six years old, the age of a first grader. They came from China in September and had a few quiet weeks on their own first, like the first days at a new school before you know where everything is. Now they're out, and people lined up to see them.
5-7.why: Two names, one zoo, a new home. At six they take the picture, and the quarantine is a quiet wait.
5-7.why_long: A six-year-old reasons from what is in front of them, so the script gives them two pandas with names and a new home, and the quarantine becomes the first quiet weeks at a new school. Nothing here needs China or 1972. Expect "can we go see them?" Honest answer: they're in Atlanta, and so are the crowds.

8-12.script: China lends pandas; it doesn't sell them. Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are on a six-year loan to Zoo Atlanta, like a library book with a due date. They arrived in late September, sat out weeks in quarantine, and now the crowds are in. Three US zoos have pandas: Atlanta, San Diego, Washington.
8-12.why: Loan, quarantine, debut: a chain. The library book is a due date at 11.
8-12.why_long: At this age they are working out rules and what follows from them, so the script hands over the chain: a loan, not a gift; weeks in quarantine first; then the doors open. The library book is a due date they already know. Expect "what happens after six years?" The story doesn't say, and say so.

13-17.script: Why does China lend pandas instead of selling them? Beijing gave Washington a pair in 1972, and pandas have been a symbol of US-China relations since. Ping Ping and Fu Shuang are in Atlanta on a six-year loan, at one of three US zoos with any. Second: is a borrowed animal a gift, or a lever?
13-17.why: Two true things: a crowd of fans, and a lever between two governments.
13-17.why_long: A teenager can hold two true things at once: a crowd lining up to see two animals, and a loan that two governments use to say something to each other. The script sets 1972 against a six-year lease and asks which one is the story. Expect "so it's just politics?" It's both, and the pandas don't know. Argue it.

5-7.a: They weren't hiding. New animals get a few quiet weeks to settle in before the crowds come. It's called quarantine.

8-12.q: Why doesn't China just give them away?
8-12.a: It lends them. These two are on a six-year agreement. The articles don't say why.

8-12.q: How many US zoos have pandas?
8-12.a: Three: Atlanta, San Diego and the National Zoo in Washington.

13-17.q: Is a panda loan really about the pandas?
13-17.a: Partly. They've been a symbol of US-China relations since 1972.

13-17.q: What happens when the six years are up?
13-17.a: The story doesn't say. The agreement runs six years.
